scenarios: Stable reopening of conventional sea routes and lower freight costs
Persistent geopolitical fragmentation and higher ton-mile costs
Eurasian rail/road logistics improvement without replacing ocean bulks
Climate, freshwater and digital-infrastructure shocks to transport resilience
contrary_evidence: Coastal or operating control of a terminal does not imply sovereignty over an international strait.
EIA chokepoint figures cover petroleum liquids and sometimes overlapping passages, not total value or volume of world merchandise.
The Middle Corridor investment forecasts and the Ferrogrão capacities are projected rather than operating freight data.
Arctic Council overall polar shipping counts do not measure Northern Sea Route intercontinental container traffic alone.
International air cargo CTK market shares cannot be compared directly with port TEU or oil-barrel statistics.
